## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Hello,

I have trouble with the reliability of the Somfy integration. I have automation that involves opening of covers at certain time, but it works randomly (maybe 1 day it works, the next day it doesn't). 

On HA I have a log ERROR that happens ~200 times a day ! : Task exception was never retrieved

Not sure it's linked with my automation issue...

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2020.12.1
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): not 100% sure but my automation works fine in 0.118.
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): HassOS 4.17
- Integration causing this issue: somfy
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/somfy/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
  client_secret: PERSONAL SECRET ID
```

review_comments:
Is there no better way than checking the "internals" of the update coordinator here? There is a risk that a behavior change of the update coordinator will break this. Doubly since there is no test.

My point is that this function doesn't control the setting of .data of the coordinator directly. I think I'd have preferred a separate variable holding the success of previous request.

I understand your doubt. The data property is part of the contract offer by the DataUpdateCoordinator: https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data 
So, it cannot be changed without any announcement. Create a subclass of the DataUpdateCoordinator would be overkill in this case IMO.

Well you could have stored a attribute on the callback function. Or used a captured nonlocal variable for the state.
But I won't require any change. Just a small concern.

Thx for merging this PR.

>Well you could have stored a attribute on the callback function. 

Can you please detailed?
